description: Maps the dos-fastapi-starter MCP server (tooling/mcp_server/) to authorized agent roles. Roster.json#mcp_tools references cluster names from this file.
wiring_note: The starter repo's MCP server is registered via the operator's project-level .mcp.json. Default invocation: `uv run --directory <starter>/tooling/mcp_server python -m dos_fastapi_mcp`. The MCP server is cwd-locked to the slot recorded in .fork-slot — set DOS_FORK_BYPASS=1 to override for cross-slot debugging.

project_status.name: Project status & fork health
project_status.purpose: Read-only inspection of starter project state, slot allocation, prerequisites, and registry agreement. Safe for any role to call as a no-op pre-flight.
project_status.notes: Run check_prerequisites + fork_status FIRST in any workflow's Phase 0. fork_status verifies cwd matches .fork-slot (avoids cross-fork mutations); list_forks enumerates parallel worktrees that share ~/.dos/forks/registry.json. If fork_status returns slot_match: false, halt the workflow — operator must investigate before code changes.

migrations.name: Alembic migration inspection
migrations.purpose: Read current revision, list migration history, detect ORM↔DB drift. Read-only — no migration generation or application via this cluster.
migrations.notes: Phase 3 (Schema) is the natural home. alembic_check is the canonical drift detector — Database role MUST run it before authoring a new migration. alembic_history shows the pending chain when investigating broken upgrades. Migration generation happens via subprocess (`cd src && uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m '...'`) — this cluster is inspection-only by design (decoupled from the app).

api_surface.name: API route inventory
api_surface.purpose: Enumerate registered FastAPI routes (path, method, summary, tags) by reading the running app's /openapi.json. Read-only.
api_surface.notes: MUST be called by API DX, Schema, Architect, Backend, Agent before authoring a new route — duplication-prevention. Frontend-equivalent (E2E) calls it to verify routes exist before authoring tests against them. Writer reads it for OpenAPI tag inventory when refreshing docs.

mailbox.name: Mailpit inbox inspection
mailbox.purpose: Read sent emails from the slot's mailpit container. E2E and TestAndValidate use this for assertion + drift checks.
mailbox.notes: E2E reaches for list_mailbox instead of HTTP-fetching mailpit's API — the MCP tool handles slot-derived port resolution automatically. Used for password-reset email flows, welcome emails, notification flows. Mailpit must be running in the slot's docker compose stack.

checks.name: Healthcheck — ruff, mypy, pytest
checks.purpose: Run the starter's defined check pipeline (ruff check, mypy, pytest). MUST in verification phases.
checks.notes: run_checks is the canonical 'is the codebase healthy?' tool — runs ruff + mypy + pytest sequentially and returns per-tool pass/fail + stderr. Verification workflows (CodeReview, TestAndValidate, BugFix Phase 4, Refactor Phase 4, DeliverFeature Phase 4) MUST invoke it. Failures route to the original implementer per the v0.5.0 ISC-failure policy.

env.name: Environment variables (slot-derived)
env.purpose: Read slot-derived env vars (API_PORT, POSTGRES_PORT, REDIS_PORT, etc.). SECRET_KEY is masked. Read-only.
env.notes: DevOps reads this to verify env-var hygiene before declaring deploy readiness. Security audits use it to verify SECRET_KEY masking and check for leaked values in non-secret keys. read_env_local does NOT expose unmasked secrets — agents must NOT attempt to coerce around the mask.
